The teaching's argument is entirely eitza-structured: (1) mingling with non-Jews creates risk of falling → guard yourself; (2) even angels could not stand in this lowly world → the challenge is real; (3) Israel has greater strength than angels and can overcome this world and cleave to the Creator → but mingling is still very hard; (4) therefore be like a strong peg, immovable in your kashrut and Jewishness.

- The concepts present (Israel, angels, non-Jews, the lowly world, a strong peg, kashrut, Jewishness, cleaving to the Creator) are all related through eitza (cause-effect, adversarial) logic, not through declared shared-nature equivalence.
